title: A monopolistically competitive yoga studio in the short run and the long run
scenario: Saltmarsh Yoga (invented) is one of many yoga studios in a city. Each studio offers its own style of classes, and a new studio can open easily. Saltmarsh maximizes profit and is earning a positive economic profit in the short run.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph for Saltmarsh Yoga showing demand, marginal revenue, marginal cost and average total cost, and show its profit-maximizing price and quantity, labeled P1 and Q1.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled graph: axes, downward-sloping D, MR below D, MC crossing ATC at the minimum of ATC.
Q1 where MR = MC and P1 on the demand curve above Q1, with P1 above ATC at Q1.
accept: dotted lines from demand to both axes

parts.sample: Price and cost on the vertical axis, Quantity on the horizontal. D slopes down with MR below it; MC crosses ATC at the lowest point of ATC. Q1 is where MR = MC; P1 is read straight up on the demand curve, above ATC at Q1.

parts.label: B

rubric.point: Shades the rectangle between P1 and ATC at Q1, from zero to Q1, completely.

parts.sample: The profit is the rectangle from P1 down to ATC at Q1, from the vertical axis out to Q1.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Show on the graph how the demand for Saltmarsh Yoga's classes changes in the long run, and in your answer explain why.

key.because: entry of new studios attracted by economic profit

rubric.point: Demand (with MR) shifts left, because economic profit attracts new studios, which take some of Saltmarsh's customers.
accept: D2 to the left of D1, explained by entry due to profit

parts.sample: Economic profit attracts new studios, and entry is easy. Each new studio takes some of Saltmarsh's customers, so Saltmarsh's demand (and its MR) shifts left, to D2.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: On a graph of Saltmarsh Yoga in long-run equilibrium, show its price and quantity, labeled P2 and Q2.

rubric.point: Q2 where MR = MC, with P2 on demand at the point where demand is tangent to ATC (P2 = ATC, zero economic profit), to the left of the minimum of ATC.
accept: the tangency of D and ATC above the MR = MC quantity

parts.sample: In the long run, demand has shifted left until it just touches ATC. Q2 is where MR = MC, and P2 is read up on demand at the tangency, where P2 = ATC, so economic profit is zero. Q2 is less than the output at the minimum of ATC: excess capacity.
